Today is September 1st, and Apple has officially handed over the CEO role from Tim Cook to John Ternus, marking the official start of a new era under Ternus's leadership.

On Apple's recently updated management page, you can see this personnel change — Ternus has been given the title of CEO, while Cook has moved to the board section, continuing in his new role as "Executive Chairman."

External expectations are that once Ternus takes the company's top position, it will signal a shift in company strategy. Compared to Cook's strength in operations management, Ternus will bring a more product-focused vision. However, such changes will take time to gradually become apparent. Ternus's first public appearance will be to introduce the all-new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra product lines at the company's fall launch event, scheduled for September 9th.

In the past, board members were listed by name only on the management page. With Cook joining the board's ranks, Apple has also expanded this section by adding individual photos of each member.

Board members include Tim Cook, Arthur Levinson, Wanda Austin, Alex Gorsky, Andrea Jung, Monica Lozano, Ron Sugar, Sue Wagner, and John Ternus (who also occupies a board seat in his capacity as CEO).
